summary: Add a provider-neutral, tenant-scoped mass catalog workspace with immutable multi-channel preview, quality/approval gates, cursor history, per-row outcomes and fail-closed connector qualification.

impacts.evidence: Selection, projections, previews, runs and kill-switch rows are organization/workspace scoped and read through forced RLS.
Evidence stores bounded digests, released media references and normalized diagnostics; raw provider payloads and secrets are rejected.
Bulk summary, cursor history, preview, apply, reconciliation and kill-switch routes are additive OpenAPI contracts.
Preview, queued-run and row-reconciliation payload schemas are versioned and contain no provider response bodies.
Field write admission uses typed connector capabilities; MCP offers the same provider-neutral dry-run only.
Migration 57 is expand-only, catalog-hashed, bounded, backup-gated by the migration framework and has tenant policies.
Authenticated scope, exact approval, actor reference, idempotency, released/safe media and emergency stop fail closed.
Mass apply requires approval bound to the exact immutable preview; clear/delete and unqualified channel writes remain blocked.
Actor, selection/input digests, before/after digests, versions, approval and per-row outcomes are retained as immutable evidence.
Stable preview/run identities, cursor history, remote observation, mismatch/unknown decisions and idempotency uniqueness cover replay safety.
No browser-controlled provider transport is introduced; real writes remain behind connector runtime and external qualification.
UI/API expose bounded counts, freshness, blockers, partitions, per-row failures and reconciliation attention without raw payloads.
Kill switch stops new intents without deleting evidence or changing PIM; recovery uses new preview/approval and reconciliation.
Core/API/MCP/migration/contract/SDK/frontend/static gates cover the repository boundary; credentialed channel evidence remains external.
